headline: Harmony Biosciences: the market is pricing WAKIX as a melting ice cube, and the pipeline comes free
subheadline: A ~$1bn drug with cover until 2030 and $775m of cash, valued at about 5x EBITDA. Lifecycle products are the swing factor
narrative: WAKIX (pitolisant) is on track for more than $1bn of net revenue in 2026. Q3 2026 sales were $269m, and full-year guidance of $1.0–1.04bn was reiterated.

Generic entry is settled with 6 of 7 ANDA filers at no earlier than March 2030 if pediatric exclusivity is granted (September 2029 without it). That leaves roughly three more years of high-margin cash flow.
The company generated $323m of free cash flow over the last 12 months and holds $775m of cash against $164m of debt. Its enterprise value is only about 1.4x revenue.
Our WAKIX-only run-off DCF ($31) is close to the share price, so the market gives almost no value to pitolisant GR (PDUFA 1 April 2027), pitolisant HD (2028) or the BP-205 orexin agonist.
A 60/40 weighting of run-off and lifecycle-success scenarios gives a $39 target (+16%). Takeda's newly approved Orzeyful is the key competitive risk.
market_pricing: At $33.76 the stock trades at about 5x EV/EBITDA and 11x earnings, against specialty-pharma peer medians of about 9x and 23x.
That discount is roughly what a 2030 patent cliff justifies. In our run-off case, revenue falls 45% in 2030 and keeps shrinking.
The stock fell after the October 2026 CEO succession news and a Q3 EPS miss on higher costs. The analyst median target is $49.50.

business.title: A one-product rare-CNS company building its next franchise
business.subtitle: WAKIX for narcolepsy today; next-generation pitolisant and an orexin agonist in development
overview: US commercial-stage pharma company based in Plymouth Meeting, Pennsylvania. It was founded by Paragon Biosciences.
WAKIX was approved by the FDA in August 2019 for narcolepsy. It is the only non-scheduled (non-controlled) treatment for excessive daytime sleepiness or cataplexy in narcolepsy.
COO Peter Anastasiou succeeds CEO Jeffrey Dayno, MD, on 1 January 2027.
Institutions own most of the free float. Insiders hold about 2%.

segments.name: WAKIX (essentially all revenue)
segments.text: Net revenue of $868.5m in 2025 and guided to $1.0–1.04bn in 2026. About 400 net patient adds a quarter.

segments.name: Pipeline
segments.text: Pitolisant GR (NDA filed, PDUFA 1 Apr 2027), pitolisant HD (Phase 3 data 2027, target PDUFA 2028), BP-205 orexin-2 agonist (Phase 1b data Q1 2027), plus EPX-100 in epilepsy.

business.source: Harmony Q3 2026 results (4 Nov 2026); Q4 2025 earnings call; company investor relations
business.financials_title: Fast growth, high margins and growing free cash flow
financial_points: Revenue grew from $438m (2022) to $868m (2025). The EBIT margin was 26–34% in each year.
Free cash flow was $348m in 2025, with almost no capex.
The Q3 2026 EPS miss came from higher costs (R&D and the commercial build) rather than demand: WAKIX added about 400 net patients.

industry.title: Narcolepsy treatment is entering a new drug class
industry.subtitle: Orexin agonists target the cause of narcolepsy type 1; WAKIX's niche is its non-controlled status
market: Narcolepsy type 1 affects about 1 in 2,000 US adults and is caused by the loss of orexin-producing neurons.
Treatment mixes wake-promoting drugs, oxybates (Jazz's Xywav, Avadel's Lumryz) and stimulants. Many patients combine therapies.
WAKIX's advantage is that it is not a controlled substance, which makes prescribing and refills simpler.

tailwinds.title: Orexin science validated
tailwinds.text: Takeda's Orzeyful approval (5 Aug 2026) validates the class Harmony is entering with BP-205.

tailwinds.title: Steady patient growth
tailwinds.text: About 400 net patient adds a quarter for WAKIX through 2026.

headwinds.title: New competition
headwinds.text: Orzeyful treats narcolepsy type 1 as a whole, which could take share from symptomatic drugs once DEA scheduling is complete.

headwinds.title: Generics
headwinds.text: Settled generic entry from March 2030 (or September 2029 without pediatric exclusivity).

industry.source: Takeda / FDA announcements (Aug 2026); Pharma Now (6 Aug 2026); Harmony filings

competition.title: Cheap against specialty-pharma peers, for a visible reason
competition.subtitle: High returns today; the debate is how much survives 2030
points: ROE was 18% in 2025 even with $775m of cash on the balance sheet. Few peers combine this growth with this margin.
Peers trade at about 9x EBITDA. Harmony trades at about 5x, because investors look past the patent cliff.
porter: Oxybates (Jazz, Avadel), modafinil/armodafinil generics, stimulants and now orexin agonists (Takeda).
Generic wake-promoters are cheap. WAKIX wins on being non-scheduled and well tolerated.
High barriers (clinical trials, rare-disease salesforce) until patents expire.
Pitolisant is licensed from Bioprojet. The product depends on that licence.
US payers. Rare-disease pricing has held up, but rebates can rise as competition grows.
competition.source: Harmony 10-Q (Q1 2026); Harmony IR; peer data from Yahoo Finance

theses.title: 1. Cash flow before 2030 covers most of the enterprise value
theses.subtitle: The patent cliff is real, but it is three-plus years away and already priced
points: WAKIX is guided to $1.0–1.04bn in 2026. With almost no capex, most operating profit converts to cash.
In our run-off case, cumulative free cash flow from 2026 to 2029 alone is more than $1bn, against an EV of about $1.37bn.
Settlements with 6 of 7 generic filers fix the earliest entry date, which reduces the risk of an early surprise.
theses.risk: The remaining patent case goes against Harmony and allows earlier generic entry, or Orzeyful cuts WAKIX growth sharply before 2030.

evidence.title: Key numbers
points: Earliest generic entry: March 2030 with pediatric exclusivity.

theses.title: 2. Lifecycle products could keep the franchise alive past 2030
theses.subtitle: Pitolisant GR and HD carry patents filed to 2044
points: Pitolisant GR (gastro-resistant) needs no dose titration. Its NDA is under FDA review, with a PDUFA date of 1 April 2027.
Pitolisant HD targets new indications. Phase 3 data are due in 2027, with a target PDUFA in 2028.
If even part of the WAKIX base moves to GR/HD before 2030, the revenue cliff becomes a slope. Our lifecycle scenario is worth $52 a share.
theses.risk: Payers and doctors treat GR as a minor reformulation and switch patients to generic pitolisant in 2030.
theses.source: Harmony Q4 2025 call and Q3 2026 release; analyst scenarios

theses.title: 3. BP-205 is a free option on the orexin class
theses.subtitle: Takeda's approval shows the class works; Harmony is aiming for best-in-class
points: Multiple-ascending-dose data for BP-205 supported once-daily dosing, with no liver, visual or significant cardiovascular events reported.
Phase 1b data in sleep-deprived volunteers are due in Q1 2027, and Phase 2 studies across several CNS indications are planned by mid-2027.
Neither of our DCF scenarios gives any value to BP-205.
theses.risk: Clinical failure or safety signals. Orexin agonists have had liver and visual side effects in earlier programmes.

evidence.title: Upcoming readouts
points: 2027: pitolisant HD Phase 3 topline; EPX-100 Phase 3 readouts.

comps.title: Harmony trades at roughly half the peer multiple on EBITDA and earnings
comps.subtitle: The gap reflects a 2030 loss of exclusivity that peers do not face to the same degree
comps.note: Peers: US commercial-stage specialty and CNS pharma with marketed products.

dcf.subtitle: Run-off case: 2026 guidance, slower growth as Orzeyful launches, then generic erosion from 2030; no pipeline value

valuation.title: The target leans on our scenarios, not on peer multiples
points: Peer multiples imply $40–86 a share, but they ignore the 2030 cliff, so we show them only as a cross-check.
Our $39 target is below the analyst median ($49.50). The difference is mostly how much value each gives the pipeline.

risks.title: Competition and the patent cliff are the risks to watch

items.risk: Orzeyful (Takeda) takes share in narcolepsy type 1
items.mitigant: WAKIX is non-scheduled and also used in type 2. Orzeyful still awaits DEA scheduling before launch.

items.risk: Earlier generic entry if the last ANDA case is lost
items.mitigant: 6 of 7 filers are already settled at 2029/2030 dates. Settlements anchor the timeline.
Our base case gives the pipeline no value, and cash of $775m funds development.

catalysts.what: New CEO Peter Anastasiou takes over.

risks.source: Harmony Q3 2026 release; Yahoo Finance earnings calendar; Takeda / FDA
